protections: URI.parse must find the authority (host) of a URL the way browsers do, so the hostname it reports is the host a browser would contact; today it only does so for an exact two-character '//' or '\\' after the scheme colon (src/URI.js:529) or an exact leading '//' (src/URI.js:516). A (variable slash/backslash runs after a web scheme) and B (the same with an upper/mixed-case scheme) are closed by the same guard, so they are ONE protection.

evidence: src/URI.js:529 only enters authority parsing when exactly the two characters after ':' become '//' after backslash replacement
src/URI.js:534-536 any other count of slashes or backslashes after a web scheme (none, one, three, mixed) is treated as a URN path, so hostname stays null while browsers resolve a host

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a scheme allowlist written in lowercase looks complete; B is a case variant of the same delimiter shape
evidence: src/URI.js:525 keeps the scheme in its original case

src/URI.js:218 protocol_expression is /i, so 'HTTP' is accepted as a scheme, but any web-scheme allowlist added next to src/URI.js:529 has to compare without regard to case, otherwise upper-case schemes get around it (this is B, 'bypass the patch')

traps.reason_to_dismiss: there is no scheme in the input, so it looks like a path-relative reference and outside a report about the scheme delimiter
evidence: src/URI.js:516 the scheme-relative branch only matches an exact '//' prefix; a leading '\\' or '/\' is not treated as an authority and falls to the scheme/path branch (src/URI.js:523, src/URI.js:542)
src/URI.js:519-521 with '///host' the extra slash is passed to parseAuthority, which reads hostname up to the first '/' (src/URI.js:560, src/URI.js:589) and gets null, while browsers resolve a host
this is a separate branch reaching parseAuthority (src/URI.js:609), so a fix written at src/URI.js:529 for scheme-prefixed input does not cover it
test/urls.js:634-641 'food:///test/file.csv' must keep hostname null and path '/test/file.csv'; collapsing slash runs for every scheme would make 'test' the host
test/urls.js:1310 'file:///foo/bar/baz.html' must keep an empty host
test/urls.js:489-496 'user:pass@www.example.org:123/...' must stay a URN with protocol 'user'; treating every 'scheme:' with no slashes as an authority breaks it
test/urls.js:537-545 '://user:pass@example.org:123/...' (empty scheme) must still parse an authority
test/urls.js:1598 mailto: and test/urls.js:1696 javascript: must stay URNs
so the authority normalisation has to be limited to web (special) schemes; the hidden coupled value is that non-web schemes keep today's behaviour

traps.reason_to_dismiss: an untrimmed or tab-containing string is not a well-formed URL, and trimming input looks like the caller's job
evidence: src/URI.js:490-526 parse never strips leading C0/space characters or embedded ASCII tab/newline before reading the scheme, while browsers do; a leading space makes the scheme fail protocol_expression (src/URI.js:526, src/URI.js:218), so the whole string becomes a path with no host
a fix at src/URI.js:529 that only looks at the delimiter does not touch this shape

masking: T2 only shows up as a separate bypass once T1 is fixed with a lowercase-only web-scheme allowlist; in the pinned code both are open through the same line (src/URI.js:529)

conflicts.what: the natural fix for T1, collapsing any slash/backslash run after any scheme into '//', makes 'test' the host of 'food:///test/file.csv' (test/urls.js:634-641) and gives 'file:///foo/bar/baz.html' a host (test/urls.js:1310)

treating 'scheme:' with no slashes as an authority (WHATWG behaviour for special schemes) applied to all schemes breaks the 'user:pass@...' URN case (test/urls.js:489-496) and mailto:/javascript: (test/urls.js:1598, test/urls.js:1696)
collapsing leading slash runs also has to keep the empty-scheme '://user:pass@host' case working (test/urls.js:537-545) and keep plain host-relative '/path' as a path
stripping all whitespace instead of only leading C0/space and ASCII tab/newline would change paths that legitimately contain encoded or literal spaces

fairness_risks: Which schemes count as 'web' is a judgement call: upstream's later fix used http, https, ftp, ws, wss; WHATWG also treats file as special, but test/urls.js:1310 and test/test.js:1461 expect 'file:///...' to keep an empty host. Hidden tests must not require file: to be normalised.

Hidden tests for T2 should use the advisory's web schemes in upper/mixed case; requiring case-folding of the stored protocol would contradict src/URI.js:525, which keeps the original case (only the comparison needs to ignore case).
T5: a test that requires interior whitespace removal would contradict legitimate paths with spaces; only leading C0/space and tab/CR/LF removal is browser-equivalent.
src/URI.min.js is a shipped build artifact of src/URI.js (package.json:52) and is not regenerated by a source fix; tests should target src/URI.js (package.json:39 main).

design.why: Four independent groups in one function, each with a different reason to dismiss: the advisory delimiter shape (T1, case variant T2 grouped with it), the no-scheme branch (T3, deepseek-type: there is no scheme so it looks out of scope), the coupled non-web-scheme values (T4, mimo-type: over-hardening breaks food:///, file:///, user:pass@ and mailto:), and untrimmed/tab input (T5, deepseek-type: it looks like the caller's job). Dropping T5 still gives three groups, but T1/T2 alone collapse into one easy regex, so T3 and T4 are what make this stack worth having. Weakness: everything lives in src/URI.js:490-546, so distance is small and one well-informed normalisation pass closes T1/T2/T3/T5 together; tiers above assume the report describes only A/B.

unverified: That A's fix (ac43ca8f80c0) and B's fix (6ea641cc8648) are not in the pinned tree is inferred from CHANGELOG.md:5 (newest entry 1.19.6) and from src/URI.js:516-539 having no scheme-normalisation regex; git history was not inspected directly.

a_fix_leaves_b_open / b_in_code_a_wrote = true come from the upstream history as I remember it (A added a case-sensitive regex for /^(https?|ftp|wss?)?:[/\\]*/ and B added the /i flag); that code is not present in the pinned checkout.

That T3 (scheme-relative slash runs) and T5 (leading whitespace, tab/newline) were fixed by later urijs advisories (1.19.9-1.19.11) is from memory; their advisory IDs were not checked and they are outside this candidate's two advisories, so origin is uncovered_upstream.
Whether any existing test has literal spaces inside a URL path (relevant to the T5 conflict) was not checked.

Not recorded as a trap: URI.ensureValidHostname compares the protocol against hostProtocols case-sensitively (src/URI.js:1084, src/URI.js:253-256), so 'HTTP' with an empty host does not throw under preventInvalidHostname. This is a case-spelling variant behind an opt-in flag (src/URI.js:212), so under the rules it is not a trap.

All other parse entry points (constructor/href at src/URI.js:1253, resource at src/URI.js:1481, origin setter at src/URI.js:1414) go through URI.parse, so they are the same fix site and not separate M1 traps.
